What is on a child's computer?

  • Tor: Tor is a browser that helps protect a user's identity. Espcially useful in repressive surveillance states. Essential learning if your child wants to go into actual journalism.

  • Virtual Machines: These are extremely useful to test software in a safe environment that does not risk the stability, security, and safety of the core operating system on your child's computer. Congratulations on buying your child a computer capable of running one, by the way.

  • Kali Linux: This is a Debian-based Linux operating system geared towards security and penetration (searching for weaknesses in security) testing of systems and networks. It is used the world over by professionals to improve the security of organizations, companies, and even UK authorities.

  • WiFi Pineapple: Congratulations! Your child is taking a healthy interest in wireless network security, and may be able to help you out with the weaknesses in your home wifi. That said, I'd be more worried about where your child came up with the $99 or $199 that these devices cost.

  • Discord: This is probably the most popular voice chat software in the world for gamers. If your child is using this, they're far more likely to be using it to rip on people in Fortnite than they are hacking. That said, as the old phrase goes, There Is No Such Thing As A Free Lunch, and I'd probably be more concerned about the privacy aspects and the platform's investors than your child learning hacking on here.

  • Metasploit: This is another framework for penetration testing systems and frameworks. Like Kali Linux, it is also used across the world by professionals who test the resilience of vital systems. In doing so, these professionals ensure the continued safe operation of the very fabric of modern life.

If you see any of these on your child's computer (with the possible exception of Discord) then congratulations! Your child is taking a healthy interest in network security!
